item.title: Texas football team unable to leave Austin for LSU game because of FAA shutdown
item.description: An American Airlines pilot flies the Texas Longhorns flag as the team arrives at Louis Armstrong International Airport on Wednesday, Dec. 27, 2023 in New Orleans, Louisiana. That decision impacted the Longhorns, who had boarded their American Airlines plane ahead of Saturday night's game at LSU. item.title: FAA ground stop does not affect Wisconsin football game vs Maryland
item.description: Wisconsin football has made it safely to Maryland as the FAA’s nationwide ground stop affects travel for many other Week 11 college football games. The Badgers ’ team charter flight took off from Madison’s Dane County Regional Airport at 1:58 p.m. CT and landed in Baltimore at 4:43 p.m. ET, per UW sports information. The FAA issued the ground stop on the afternoon of Nov. 13, citing an air traffic control issue that led to extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns . U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a tweet that it is a communication issue that impacts all air traffic control centers. Other Big Ten road teams were not as fortunate as the Badgers . Minnesota, Purdue and Washington have been affected, according to ESPN’s Pete Thamel , ahead of their respective games against Penn State, Iowa and Michigan State. A Big Ten spokesman told Thamel that all of the league’s officials are on site and not affected by the FAA ground stop. This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: FAA ground stop does not affect Wisconsin football game vs Maryland

item.title: Lynch: Remembering Dan Hicks | Opinion
item.description: A few years back, I sat next to Dan Hicks in an Orlando steakhouse talking about working in television, which he’d been doing to acclaim for decades and I, stutteringly, for a hot minute. I asked a question that I often put to accomplished companions at dinner: what was the worst screw-up from which he learned the most? He didn’t hesitate to search for an answer. Dan recalled one of his earliest assignments in golf for NBC Sports, at what was then known as the Bob Hope Chrysler Classic. He was emceeing the trophy presentation on the 18th green, during which he was to be alongside the tournament host, who even then was well stricken in years. Ahead of the ceremony, he received a final word of advice from Tommy Roy, the longtime NBC golf producer. “Do not, under any circumstances,” Roy told him, “lose the microphone.” Sitting in that restaurant years later, Hicks gave a comical account of a tug-of-war that went entirely unnoticed by viewers. As he welcomed in Hope, Dan hovered his stick mic closer to the legendary entertainer so that he might offer a few words. Hope attempted to take it. Dan held on. Almost imperceptibly, Hope tugged a little harder. Smile fixed, Dan kept a Vulcan death grip. In the end, he lost out to guile and experience when Hope snatched the mic and turned to address the crowd. Dan described hearing an anguished, guttural groan in his earpiece from the production truck. “Uggghhhhh.” What remained of the broadcast would now run on Bob Hope’s schedule, not Tommy Roy’s. That was the last time Dan lost control of the microphone, which he wielded with assurance and diligence until his unexpected passing on Nov. 11 at the age of 64. His was a career that seemed to have precious few screw-ups that might be rendered fodder for laughs over dinner, but he’d probably argue the over on that. Others have memories that are more personal, but equally enduring. My relationship with Dan was one of casual friendship. He’d text occasionally about a column he’d read or show he’d seen, or to joke about Brad Faxon’s fashion sense (sorry, Brad!). I’d study him to see what I could learn, admitting to him that I felt like a 15-handicap chop trying to borrow moves from Scottie Scheffler. We’d see each other a handful of times each year walking the range at tournaments, and at the Payne Stewart Award dinner that he hosted. A few times we went from there to Nan’s, a Thai restaurant in Atlanta where Dan was as well-known, as comfortable and as loved as in his own kitchen at home. Those dinners were like every interaction with Dan: flush with sharp observations, memorable storytelling and riotously funny one-liners. But what I’ll remember most from those times is his unfailing encouragement. He was a one-man tide intent on lifting all boats. Everyone felt a little better about themselves after time in his company. That’s rare in a business riven with insecurities and egos. He was a Colossus in sports media, but you wouldn’t have known it from his demeanor. Dan knew his place in the firmament, but had no compulsion to remind anyone else of theirs. But more than the applause or the accolades or the Emmys, he was just a good hang, and for that alone he will be sorely missed. His grip on the microphone has been loosened for the first time since Bob Hope wrestled it from him all those years ago. item.title: Philip Rivers’ introductory press conference set for Monday
item.description: RALEIGH, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 29: Former NC State quarterback Philip Rivers attends the game between the North Carolina Tar Heels and the NC State Wolfpack at Carter-Finley Stadium on November 29, 2025 in Raleigh, North Carolina. (Photo by Lance King/Getty Images) | Getty Images NC State made it official today that Philip Rivers will be the football program’s next head coach, and he will be introduced on Monday afternoon at 1:30 p.m. ET. ACC Network will carry the press conference live. Rivers’ deal with NC State is reportedly worth $3.25 million annually over five seasons, and the buyout is his salary multiplied by the number of years remaining on his deal. This part of the risk, at least, is relatively inexpensive. From NC State’s press release : “I am humbled and honored to be the next head football coach at NC State University,” Rivers said. “In many ways, I feel like I’m coming home. This is where it all began for me as an 18-year-old kid from Alabama, and now to return to this great place as head coach is beyond words. “I gave it everything I had here as a player for 51 games and I will give it everything I have as the coach. There’s no denying that this is going to take hard work, but we’re not scared of hard. I look forward to getting after it every single day with an unbelievable coaching staff and a group of players who are dedicated to relentlessly pursuing victory.” Philip is one of the most competitive guys out there, and hopefully he can channel that in the right way in this new position, because it’s going to be a lot for him. As with all new coaching hires, I’ll be cautiously optimistic until proven otherwise.

item.title: Senne Lammens opens up on Michael Carrick’s sack
item.description: Senne Lammens opens up on Michael Carrick’s sack Michael Carrick paid the ultimate price for Manchester United’s dismal start to the season, with the Red Devils languishing in 18th position in the Premier League after winning only once so far. The former head coach received his marching orders amid complaints about the squad’s poor fitness levels and tactical blunders. INEOS’ role in this whole fiasco cannot be taken lightly, as they failed to back the Englishman in the summer. Add to this key players underperforming, and such a scenario was bound to happen. One of last season’s top performers , goalkeeper Senne Lammens, has struggled to replicate that form , with the Belgian failing to keep a single clean sheet in the league. Lammens on INEOS’ call to sack Carrick He arguably had the worst game of his United career so far against Aston Villa, in what turned out to be Carrick’s final game in charge. The 24-year-old was asked about Carrick’s dismissal after his country’s international friendly against Türkiye. He explained that INEOS’ decision was a tough pill to swallow for the whole squad, which had shown through recent results that they were fully behind the former United midfielder. “Yes, these are difficult weeks. I’m not going to lie about that,” he admitted. “Of course, as a Manchester United team, we need to do better. Why United were forced to sack Carrick “Now the manager has been sacked. It’s obviously a difficult time, both for me and for the whole team. We were all behind him.” After the Bournemouth debacle, United’s co-owners had reportedly handed Carrick a three-game ultimatum . It started in disastrous fashion. The 20-time English league champions showed promise in the first half against Chelsea before Lisandro Martínez single-handedly dragged his team down. A trademark comeback in the Champions League against AS Roma followed, and despite a come-from-behind 4-4 draw against Aston Villa, INEOS decided to pull the plug. Mauricio Pochettino has a mountain to climb, with INEOS reportedly expecting European football at the end of the season despite the fact that the Argentine is inheriting a weak and broken squad . online polls

item.title: Joshua Kimmich insists he has “no problems” with his ankle after dangerous tackle
item.description: Photo by Christian Charisius/picture alliance via Getty Images Joshua Kimmich received a heavy tackle from substitute Vanja Dragojević in the 76th minute of Germany’s 3-1 UEFA Nations League victory against Serbia. Kimmich went down clutching his ankle leaving German — and especially Bayern — fans holding their breath. The German captain managed to finish the game. However, many remained concerned there could have been some damage to the midfielder’s joint. In a post-match interview, Kimmich eased worries. When asked whether the knock he took would be an issue ahead of Germany’s high-stakes clash against the Netherlands on Monday, Kimmich insisted he had “no problems” with his ankle. “No, there are no problems at all,” said the 31-year-old midfielder (via @iMiaSanMia ). Bayern Munich already have a laundry list of injuries. The last thing Die Rekordmeister needed was an injury to their midfield lynchpin. Thankfully, it appears Kimmich is healthy. However, It does remind one of how costly these international breaks can be. One bad challenge is all it takes to end a player’s season. Join the conversation! item.title: Cowboys’ 4-5 Record Shows Disappointing Halfway Point
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys reached the halfway mark of the 2026 season with a record that leaves fans asking hard questions. A recent win over the Indianapolis Colts kept playoff hopes alive, but the team sits at 4-5 overall. This standing places them in a precarious spot within the conference race. The victory did lift the team up three spots in the NFC standings, per Blogging The Boys . Yet, the loss to Arizona and Tampa Bay earlier this year still weighs heavily on their resume. Those two defeats make it vital that the Cowboys stay ahead of those rivals moving forward. The Standings Reality Check Dallas currently holds the tenth spot in the big picture of the 2026 NFC Playoff Standings according to Blogging The Boys. A drop to 4-6 is likely if they lose to the conference-leading 49ers this week. Such a slide could allow teams with 3-6 records to creep back above Dallas in the rankings. It is only Week 10, so there is still ample time to rectify the situation, per the same report. However, the margin for error has vanished for a team with big-market expectations. High Stakes Against San Francisco The upcoming matchup features the conference-leading 49ers visiting AT&T Stadium on Sunday. This game is a critical test for a squad that has struggled to maintain consistency. The pressure is on to prove that the recent win over Indy was more than a fluke. Fans need to see a team that can handle a top-tier opponent without falling apart. The Cowboys must win this game to keep their name in the hunt for a wild card spot. According to Blogging The Boys, unless a massive upset occurs, a likely fall to 4-6 might let certain 3-6 squads surpass them in the rankings. The Cowboys host the conference-leading 49ers this week, which sets the stage for a must-win scenario. A loss here would deepen the crisis for a roster that promised more before the season started. The clock is ticking on the 2026 campaign, and the next game defines the rest of it. The Cowboys are currently 4-5 (2-4) in the 2026 NFC standings, per Blogging The Boys.

item.title: Friday Night Happy Hour: Division showdown edition
item.description: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images | Getty Images Welcome back to BTSC’s Friday night open thread: The Steelers take on the Bengals this week for the AFC North lead. What are your thoughts, feelings, and predictions heading into this game and coming off the bye week? Ja’Marr Chase acknowledged the Bengals and Steelers are rivals, but then said they weren’t anywhere as close as rivals as the Bengals and the Chiefs. Sure it’s petty, but who doesn’t like a little smack talk with a division rival before a big game. What one liners do you have for the Bengals? Who, besides the Ravens, do you think are the Steelers top rivals presently? The Steelers didn’t make any moves at the trade deadline. Last chance to share your thoughts on that. I’m personally glad they didn’t trade away picks for what would likely be a rental player. But what was your reaction? Looking at the AFC playoff picture, it mostly seems set. The Ravens or Texans could surprise in the second half, possibly, and I don’t have a ton of faith in the Raiders or Browns. But those are the only teams on the outside right now that could get in. Given that, how do you think the Steelers stack up in the AFC playoffs right now? Could they finally end the drought? Song of the Night: “A Decade Under the Influence” – Taking Back Sunday

item.title: Cowboys aggressiveness on offense must be turned up vs. 49ers
item.description: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images After two straight weeks of early window kickoffs in which the Dallas Cowboys had to fight, claw, scratch, and get knocked down to go 1-1 against the Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts, they play in the Sunday late afternoon window against the San Francisco 49ers. Both teams are off a win, which puts the Cowboys right back in a position they’ve been time and time again and failed in nearly every time, trying to win consecutive games under Brian Schottenheimer. The Cowboys can’t afford to spin their wheels much longer if they want to make this season mean something though. This 49ers matchup is exactly that opportunity for the Cowboys, so let’s get to how they can pull off the upset. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the San Francisco 49ers if… …they win on 1st down on both offense and defense. Think for a second about how many NFL offenses are truly earning the label of “elite”, “scary”, or “explosive” right now, then without looking at any other metrics or analytics consider the top four tiers in the first downs per play category. They are the Bills, 49ers, Lions, and Bengals tied for first, the Cowboys in second, and the Jaguars and Rams in third just ahead of the Patriots and Chiefs. Also among these teams, the 49ers, Lions, and Bills are in the top five for fewest third downs faced per game. The Patriots, Chiefs, Jags, and Bengals are all virtually tied with the Bills to round out the top nine. Then there are the 14th ranked Cowboys, much closer to teams like the Steelers, Texans, and Browns – none of which have the QB situation Dallas does that should be keeping them out of this not-so-great company. This is a main culprit why they feel like outliers on the elite, scary, or explosive list while the other offenses are much more deserving. For even more evidence that the Cowboys offense is all about Dak right now, and that Prescott should be getting way more help than he is from all directions, there’s the fact two of the three touchdown drives last week at the Colts came in two minute situations before halftime and at the end of the game. item.content:encoded: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images After two straight weeks of early window kickoffs in which the Dallas Cowboys had to fight, claw, scratch, and get knocked down to go 1-1 against the Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts, they play in the Sunday late afternoon window against the San Francisco 49ers. Both teams are off a win, which puts the Cowboys right back in a position they’ve been time and time again and failed in nearly every time, trying to win consecutive games under Brian Schottenheimer. The Cowboys can’t afford to spin their wheels much longer if they want to make this season mean something though. This 49ers matchup is exactly that opportunity for the Cowboys, so let’s get to how they can pull off the upset. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the San Francisco 49ers if… …they win on 1st down on both offense and defense. Think for a second about how many NFL offenses are truly earning the label of “elite”, “scary”, or “explosive” right now, then without looking at any other metrics or analytics consider the top four tiers in the first downs per play category. They are the Bills, 49ers, Lions, and Bengals tied for first, the Cowboys in second, and the Jaguars and Rams in third just ahead of the Patriots and Chiefs. Also among these teams, the 49ers, Lions, and Bills are in the top five for fewest third downs faced per game. The Patriots, Chiefs, Jags, and Bengals are all virtually tied with the Bills to round out the top nine. Then there are the 14th ranked Cowboys, much closer to teams like the Steelers, Texans, and Browns – none of which have the QB situation Dallas does that should be keeping them out of this not-so-great company. This is a main culprit why they feel like outliers on the elite, scary, or explosive list while the other offenses are much more deserving. For even more evidence that the Cowboys offense is all about Dak right now, and that Prescott should be getting way more help than he is from all directions, there’s the fact two of the three touchdown drives last week at the Colts came in two minute situations before halftime and at the end of the game. The Cowboys need much more than just Prescott to be at their absolute best against the 49ers, but fairly or not will also need #4 to be among the players that elevates their game this week as well. The best path towards doing so is much more early down aggressiveness and the Cowboys embracing what they do best by throwing the ball to CeeDee Lamb, and hopefully George Pickens, not just on third down, but all the time. Without Jake Ferguson for this game, one of the things the Cowboys are going to have an incredibly difficult time doing is persuading the 49ers defense out of loading the box. They don’t have the middle of the field threat to get behind these stacked looks, especially considering the freakish coverage ability to all parts of the field from Fred Warner. Dallas will still need to find it’s times to run the ball and doing so well on early downs would also be huge, but staying in spread looks and letting Prescott make the right decision should be their bread and butter. The 49ers use motion on 71.5% of their offensive plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL. The Cowboys have allowed +0.11 EPA per play against motion, LAST in the NFL. @DLLS_Cowboys pic.twitter.com/Gq8Gr9vUrg — John Andersen (@AndersenJA) November 11, 2026 This could also allow them to use some tempo to their advantage, getting to the line quickly to give them time to use motions, something the 49ers offense is going to do a ton of to the Cowboys defense, and Cowboys offense would be wise to try to give it back. On defense, the Cowboys need to do everything they can to limit the vast amount of plays 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan can get to at all times. If Christian McCaffrey is breaking tackles and getting considerable gains on first downs all game, the 49ers are simply too talented and well-coached to be stopped. They will toy with Christian Parker’s defense when ahead of the chains with short, intermediate, and deep layered passes. There’s also the element of Brock Purdy’s effectiveness scrambling outside of the pocket, another area Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark will have to step up in pushing the pocket and keeping contain. A complete game in both run and pass defense from the Cowboys front will give them a chance to replicate what the Atlanta Falcons did to the 49ers as the only team to beat them this season. How often QBs have had perfectly blocked plays and their EPA on those plays pic.twitter.com/Erv2iR2BIO — Jrfortgang (@throwthedamball) November 11, 2026 The Dallas Cowboys will lose to the San Francisco 49ers if… …they are horribly outcoached. Even though the disparity in records is obvious in this game between the 7-1 49ers and 4-5 Cowboys, if the game was going to solely be decided by the players on the field, I think many fans on both sides would be expecting a much closer game than they currently are. The biggest gripe from Cowboys fans when it comes to things they’re not looking forward to the most about this toughest game of the season to date is how likely it feels the 49ers coaching staff will run laps around the Cowboys staff, and separate even more on the scoreboard as a result of it. Play Caller Tendencies 🎮 The NFC North is the only division where every offensive play caller has a positive rating. The AFC North, AFC East, and NFC West are close behind, each with at least three play callers in positive territory. pic.twitter.com/kmd5AduJDw — Steven Patton (@PattonAnalytics) November 11, 2026 This chart shows that Schottenheimer is lacking creativity in his offensive formations/plays, while Shanahan is uplifting the 49ers with his usual masterclass at taking a roster hammered by injuries and still finding a way to win. The Cowboys have already lost to four of the coaches that presently rank above Schottenheimer on this chart, play the 49ers this Sunday, then still have to play the Jaguars and Seahawks in December. The only win for Schotty against a coach above him on this list is the one directly above him by the smallest of margins, Nick Caley with the Texans. The Cowboys are finding themselves outcoached all too often right now. The Cowboys have the talent to compete with this 49ers team, and they have everything left to play for in the NFC East. If they come out and continue to have communication issues on both sides of the ball, call plays like they’re playing to not lose instead of playing to win, and shoot themselves in the foot with egregious penalties, it will be all most fans need to see that this season is doomed to look like year one under Schottenheimer and fall short of the playoffs again. A Cowboys head coach that’s had the chance to work with a healthy Dak Prescott has never had as little success as Schottenheimer is now, and Prescott has not beaten the 49ers since being with the coach that drafted him Jason Garrett in 2017. The chance for this QB-HC duo to have a real signature moment is right there for the taking in week ten if the Cowboys play their best game of the season, a challenge the Dallas coaching staff needs to rise to instead of wilting under the pressure of.

item.title: Brajan Gruda on his dream debut goal for Germany
item.description: BELGRADE, SERBIA - NOVEMBER 13: Brajan Gruda of Germany celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Serbia and Germany at Rajko Mitic Stadium on November 13, 2026 in Belgrade, Serbia. (Photo by Maja Hitij/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brajan Gruda is in dreamland. The 22-year-old German forward had his breakout a few seasons ago for Mainz — earning rave reviews from Bayern Munich and national team legend Thomas Müller at the time — but his career has taken a circuitous path since. His big move to England did not pay off, at least not quickly, and after a nondescript season-and-a-half at Brighton, Gruda found himself back in the Bundesliga, this time on loan at RB Leipzig. But this year, it is all starting to come together. New Germany boss Jürgen Klopp has been keen on incorporating the dynamic attacker’s skills into the men’s national team setup; Gruda narrowly missed a call-up in September due to injury to Klopp’s super-sized squad. But his season at Leipzig has been promising — two goals and five assists across all competitions. When Klopp trimmed the roster for his second international period, Gruda still made the cut. Now he is taking his break and running with it. Friday against Serbia in a quiet, rain-sodden Belgrade stadium (largely devoid of fans owing to a UEFA spectator ban for the match), Gruda earned a place in Klopp’s XI for his Germany debut. He left having terrorized the Serbian defenses with a man-of-the-match performance, and collecting a dazzling goal after dribbling halfway down the pitch. All while being the man to don the #10 shirt — which he is fitting very, very well in. “Jo [Kimmich] was on the ball, and with my first touch, I moved inside,” Gruda said of his higlight-reel moment (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). “There was so much space that I thought I had to take advantage of it. And the fact that they weren’t closing me down was good for me too, so I simply made the most of it. It was instinct. I don’t think too much when I’m dribbling. I just do it. I don’t think there’s really time to think anyway. It just happens. That’s it.” Gruda’s effort put Germany up 3-0 after just 50 minutes, proving to be the dagger en route to a commanding 3-1 win . The way he’s playing, there is sure to be much more to come. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: New, improved notifications system! item.title: Kenneth Walker Injury Threatens Chiefs’ Rushing Momentum
item.description: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Kenneth Walker III, the running back for the Kansas City Chiefs, missed Friday practice because of a sore groin, casting doubt on his availability for Sunday’s game. The team lacks a top rusher after an injury created a gap in the lineup. In his first season with the squad, Walker has accumulated 872 rushing yards, trailing the league lead by just eight yards. His per-game average of 109 yards leads the entire NFL, so his absence would be a major blow if he cannot play. Reid Backs the Rookie Head coach Andy Reid knows the pressure is on, yet he remains calm about the backup plan. Reid stated that the team will monitor Walker’s condition leading into Sunday, but he is not panicking about the loss of production. “He’s going to play anyway, whether Ken’s there or not,” Reid said regarding the game plan. The coach has total faith in the young players ready to step up if the starter cannot go. “Everybody has confidence in him,” Reid added when asked about the depth chart. Rookie Emmett Johnson is the name on everyone’s lips if Walker sits out. Johnson is a fifth-round pick out of Nebraska who has already shown he can handle big touches. He has rushed for 111 yards and a touchdown on just 26 carries this season. The rookie also secured 14 catches for 237 yards and another score, demonstrating he is a complete back. Should Walker be unable to play this weekend, Johnson stands ready to assume a larger workload. Other Keys to the Game The offense has other pieces moving into place for the trip to Atlanta. Wide receiver Josh Downs plans to participate days after being traded from Indianapolis. Just before the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, the Chiefs acquired Downs from the Colts. Reid praised the new receiver’s quick learning curve, noting, “I thought he did a nice job for what we asked him to do, to digest everything in a couple days.” Health concerns linger elsewhere, but the team expects wide receiver Xavier Worthy to be available after he left the previous game with a hamstring injury. The New Haven Register reports that the squad still lacks wide receiver Tyquan Thornton, who sits on injured reserve because of a dislocated ankle. Reid called Downs a smart kid who knows how to play. The Chiefs face the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1 p.m. ET in Mercedes-Benz Stadium. According to the Associated Press, Walker has participated in one fewer game this year than the Atlanta Falcons running back, producing a distinctive statistic for the matchup. Walker has caught 22 balls for 172 yards and four touchdowns, showing his value as a receiver out of the backfield. The team will see how Walker’s sore groin holds up before making a final call on his status. “We’ll see. He’s not one to say something like that (without meaning it),” Reid said.

Photo: Christian Charisius/dpa - IMPORTANT NOTICE: In accordance with the regulations of the Bundesliga and the DFB (German Football Association), it is prohibited to use or allow the use of photographs taken in the stadium and/or during the game in the form of sequential images and/or video-like photo sequences. (Photo by Christian Charisius/picture alliance via Getty Images) In front of a largely empty Rajko Mitic Stadium in Belgrade, Germany came away with a 3-1 win over Serbia in their first of two UEFA Nations League matches during this month’s international break. An own goal from Srđan Babić in the third minute well before his consolation goal in the 56th minute opened the scoring for Germany in what was a dominant first half display aside from a spirited end from the Serbians to the first 45 minutes. Florian Wirtz added a second for Die Mannschaft in the 14th minute after tapping in from point blank range after what looked like keeper Vanja Milinković-Savić getting a hand to initial chip attempt. Brajan Gruda rounded out the scoring for Germany in the 50th minute with a moment of individual brilliance having made a 40-yard run with the ball at his feet and Jürgen Klopp had quite the smile on his face when cameras panned to the German dugout after the goal. Gruda’s goal wrapped a bow on what was Klopp’s second win since becoming Germany manager and a win that keeps the Germans in third place in Nations League group B ahead of the clash against the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday night. The Dutch will be heading to Berlin on the heels of a comprehensive 7-0 win over Greece in Amsterdam as Xavi Hernández really seems to have found his way with the Dutch national team. After the win over Serbia, Joshua Kimmich was asked whether or not he’ll be going into the match against the Netherlands with the mentality of a cup final as Germany fight to get into the second spot in the group. “Yes, absolutely. I think we actually have to win, given the current situation in the group. So we’re really looking forward to the game,” he said (via @iMiaSanMia ). A win alone over the Dutch wouldn’t guarantee second spot in the group for Germany, as they would also need Greece to not defeat Serbia in Volos. item.title: Jonathan Taylor Says Trade Talks Are Above His Pay Grade
item.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) waves to fans as he leaves the field Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, after losing a game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Despite intense speculation connecting them to Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, the New York Giants made no moves by the NFL trade deadline. Per reports, while a second-round and a fifth-round pick were reportedly offered, the transaction failed to complete before the deadline arrived. As a 2-7 Indianapolis Colts member, Taylor stayed put and expressed his views clearly during his initial media session after the deadline expired. Taylor Takes The High Road Speaking with reporters, Taylor was blunt when asked about not getting traded to a contender like the Giants. He told the media that trade decisions are way above his pay grade and that he is glad he does not have to make those hard calls. Taylor stated that his only job is to come in and make sure he is at his best each and every single day for his coaches and teammates. He told reporters, according to Heavy.com , “I would hate to be in that situation. But I know that they have a vision and a plan for it.” While Giants fans might have wanted a blockbuster move, Taylor seems content to just execute the plan the Colts have set out for him right now. He emphasized that the best thing to help the team is executing and getting a win versus Miami. Why The Colts Held Firm It is easy to wonder why the Colts did not trade their best remaining player when they are sitting at 2-7 and have no first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. ESPN’s Dan Graziano stated that Indianapolis felt no urgency to trade since Taylor is signed through the 2028 season. The front office clearly decided that keeping their star running back was more valuable than the premium picks they could have gotten in return. Several weeks prior, the Colts traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and on Tuesday they also parted ways with wide receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs. Unlike other key departures, Taylor was not moved, and he never asked for a trade or stated a desire to leave. This silence suggests he is willing to ride it out in Indy while the team rebuilds around him. Giants Find Value Elsewhere The Giants missed out on the biggest name at the deadline, but they did not mortgage their future for an overpriced player. GM Joe Schoen stood pat because the asking prices for defensive tackles were too steep and the team only has five picks in the 2027 draft. Rather than exchanging picks, the organization noted that rookie defensive lineman Bobby Jamison-Travis has gained more playing time and recorded a 77.5 run‑defense grade versus the Texans, per reports.

item.title: Rangers Interest In Sato Faces $100M Price Tag Reality
item.description: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images The Texas Rangers are looking at Teruaki Sato, but the price might be too high for this specific roster. The Athletic’s Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon note the club is pursuing the NPB star. They also note that Texas is a long shot given the expected cost. The Rangers have been focused on cutting costs rather than spending big on new free agents. Sato is a left-handed hitter with massive power who just turned 28. This season, he produced 39 home runs with the Hashin Tigers, following a 40-home run campaign the prior year. His slash line was .306/.383/.609 across 614 plate appearances. MLB Trade Rumors predicted a five-year, $80 million deal, while other estimates put his value over $100 million. The signing team must also pay a posting fee based on the contract value. The Payroll Problem The money is the biggest issue for a team that already pays too much. MLB Trade Rumors states the Rangers finished the 2026 season carrying a $192.8 million cash payroll. Their luxury tax number hit $218.7 million. They are projected to spend around $175 million in cash and $194 million on the tax next year. Chris Young, president of baseball operations, indicated payroll figures will remain comparable to this year’s level. Sato would likely need a contract in the nine-figure range. The Rangers have big obligations to Corey Seager, Jacob deGrom, and Nathan Eovaldi. They might not have the room to add another huge salary. The team could try to trade MacKenzie Gore or deal Jake Burger to create some short-term space. Even then, a nine-figure deal is a stretch for a team trying to balance the books. Does He Fit The Roster? There are other questions about where Sato would play. He has played mostly third base in Japan, but scouts think he projects more as a corner outfielder. The Rangers are set up nicely at third base with Josh Jung. They do have an opening at designated hitter since Joc Pederson is testing free agency. A left fielder might be acquired while Wyatt Langford continues playing center field. Some teams worry about his hit tool translating to the majors. He struck out at a 26.7 percent rate in Japan, where the pitching is weaker than in Major League Baseball. Hitters from the NPB usually strike out more often when they come over. Sato likely faces a 30 percent strikeout rate upon playing in the US. That is a tradeoff teams make if he hits 30 or more homers. The Rangers might be watching just in case the market collapses like it did for Munetaka Murakami a year ago. There is no harm in doing the scouting work without spending the money yet.

item.title: Football Daily | Taking a brief minute to remember Pierre Sage’s impact at Crystal Palace
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! So farewell then, Pierre Sage . Many coaches leave under a cloud, not many have their departures completely obscured by the foul, retch-inducing one emanating from another team’s managerial circus, but such was Sage’s fate . The news section of Crystal Palace’s website helpfully tells you the amount of time it might take you to read each story it links through to. For example it should take four minutes or so to get through Tuesday’s “On this day: five big Crystal Palace birthdays”. “England: I love a knee slide!” will take you five. “Prize draw: be a mascot for our next [Bigger Vase] tie!” is a two-minute job. The statement informing the world of Sage’s exit? One minute. Eighty-three words. By way of illustration, the word “words” was the 84th of this paragraph. Just because the man’s French doesn’t mean his exit should be marked with a shrug. As I have been away at a conference, giving a presentation that the MC described as ‘sobering’, I’ve missed the last few days of football, so I was very sad to read about the passing of the great Danny Kelly . Others are far better placed to give tributes to the great man, but for younger generations who can’t comprehend the football cultural significance, Baker and Kelly represented the peak of football phone-ins. Before it became people ranting and raving about wanting the manager sacked as they’ve lost a few games or wanting the club to spend another few hundred million pounds on yet more players, it was about football supporters and supporting, from fans who actually went to games. Their peak was on BBC Radio in the 1990s, and there are too many examples of their greatness, but if I had to pick one, just one to illustrate it, it would, of course, be Gordon the Dundee United supporter and his bow tie . Rest in Peace, Danny Kelly. You gave us such joy” – Noble Francis. As they no longer seem to be ‘Dr Tottenham’, I was wondering if they had maybe passed the soubriquet on. I think the England cricket team has provided the answer (again)” – Andrew Parker. item.title: Why Chelsea and Manchester City’s WSL clash is not as season-defining as you think
item.description: Neither side have lost in the league yet but a more competitive division should take title race to the wire There was a time when the games between the top three – traditionally Chelsea, Manchester City and Arsenal – were title-deciders. Where every point taken off a title rival was key. Such was the gap in investment and quality between those teams and the rest of the Women’s Super League, it was extremely rare that points would be dropped to teams outside that elite clique. As the WSL has grown in investment, profile and size, that narrative has started to shift a little. The investment gap is still large from the top to the bottom of the league. But increased investment among the best of the rest and even among those teams further down the table, as well as an increase in high-quality coaches with the tactical and technical vision to get more from players, is having an impact. item.title: The beautiful game: revived art prize gives football its creative due once more | Emma John
item.description: Football and the art world have long remained distant but the breadth of entries for this year’s award reveals a healthy revival It may be the Beautiful Game, but in its early decades football was a rare subject for artists. The Italian Futurist Umberto Boccioni whirled an athlete’s body into a vortex of movement in his 1913 painting Dynamism of a Soccer Player . You can see one of the earliest fine art depictions of a match – a smoggy, factory-adjactent scene called Any Wintry Afternoon in England – at the Manchester Art Gallery. If 1930s abstraction is more your thing, you can enjoy decoding the geometric shapes in Kazimir Malevich’s Painterly Realism of a Football Player – Color Masses in the 4th Dimension. I’m guessing the small green pea shape is a ball. These, in any case, were exceptions. In 1953 the Football Association launched an art prize, backed by the newly formed Arts Council: the winning works included Going To The Match by LS Lowry, with its crowds flocking to Bolton Wanderers’ then home ground, Burnden Park. An exhibition of the submissions, Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country and the FA secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, said he hoped it would finally break the barrier between those two worlds. item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tactics Sign up for our free newsletter here Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. item.title: That’s a Mora: Rodrigo and Roma rise with Lazio to give Eternal City new life | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Roma and Lazio have both made unbeaten starts to the Serie A season, giving those in the Italian capital dreams of a Scudetto After nine games in 28 days, Gian Piero Gasperini finally got a moment to pause and reflect on Sunday night. The Roma manager was back in Liguria, where he worked for the best part of a decade across two stints at Genoa, to collect an award from Stelle Nello Sport – an association formed to promote sport in the region – celebrating his career achievements and commitment to courageous attacking football. The timing worked out well. Gasperini’s Roma thumped Sassuolo 3-0 on Saturday, bouncing back from a midweek defeat against Manchester United . That result meant the Giallorossi had scored 31 times in 11 Serie A games. In the past 65 years only two Italian teams – the Juventus and Napoli sides of 2017-18 – had made a more prolific start to a top-flight campaign. More importantly, Roma’s victory meant they remained undefeated in domestic competition this season. Just like their neighbours Lazio, who drew 1-1 away against Napoli in the early kick-off on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
